answer: Resistance comes from staked identity with slashable collateral: an agent earns trust only by locking a bond and collecting signed attestations from already-trusted peers. To pass off a token named onyx, a second named bridge, and a third named tundra as distinct voters, an attacker must post three independent bonds and recruit three separate guarantors, then risk losing every bond if the cluster is caught. The cost therefore grows with each fake identity instead of staying flat, so a large Sybil army becomes unaffordable.
